steps.scene: You're stopped at a pelican crossing. The red light changes to flashing amber, and one person is still walking across.

options.text: Move off — flashing amber means go
Give way until they're clear, then go if nobody else is crossing
Sound your horn to hurry them along

question.explanation: Flashing amber means give way to anyone on the crossing. You move off only once it's clear.

a.label: Pelican
a.body: Has a flashing amber phase: give way to anyone still on the crossing, then go.

b.label: Puffin
b.body: Sensors watch the crossing and hold the red. Steady amber follows green, as at normal lights.

question.prompt: Which colour follows the green signal at a puffin crossing?

options.text: Flashing amber, the same as a pelican
Steady amber
Red, straight away

question.explanation: A puffin holds its red while people are still crossing, so it never needs a flashing-amber phase.

a.label: Pelican & puffin
a.body: For people on foot. A cyclist has to get off and push across.

b.label: Toucan
b.body: A wider crossing shared by people and cyclists — cyclists may ride straight across.

question.prompt: Which crossing may cyclists ride across without getting off?

options.text: A toucan crossing
A puffin crossing
A pelican crossing

question.explanation: Two can cross a toucan. Expect bikes arriving much faster than walking pace, from either side.

steps.title: Someone waiting at a zebra
steps.body: A zebra has no lights to protect it. Slow down and be ready to stop as soon as you see someone waiting to cross.

question.prompt: Someone is waiting at the kerb of a zebra crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Be ready to slow down and stop to let them cross
Carry on — they don't count until they've stepped out
Stop only if they raise a hand to you

question.explanation: Once someone is on a zebra you MUST give way — and you should give way to anyone waiting to cross.

steps.wrongBelief: Waving a pedestrian across a crossing is the polite thing to do.

question.prompt: Why should you never wave someone across?

options.text: It's fine, as long as you've checked your mirrors first
Another vehicle may be coming that you can't see or stop
Pedestrians aren't allowed to accept signals from drivers

question.explanation: Your wave can send someone into the path of a vehicle overtaking you. Wait, and let them decide when to go.

steps.repairNote: Never wave or flash anyone across. Wait quietly — they, not you, can judge the whole road.

steps.title: Never overtake at a crossing
steps.body: On the zigzag approach you must not overtake the vehicle nearest the crossing, or one that has stopped to let people cross.

question.prompt: The car ahead has stopped to let someone cross. What should you do?

options.text: Wait behind it — you must not overtake at a crossing
Pass it if the crossing looks clear from where you are
Sound your horn so the driver moves on

question.explanation: You can't see what the stopped driver can see. Overtaking there is how people on crossings get hit.

steps.scene: Traffic ahead is queuing. If you move up with it you'll end up stopped right on a pedestrian crossing.

options.text: Move up anyway, to keep the queue tight
Stop before the crossing and leave it clear
Use the zigzags to get past the queue

question.explanation: Never queue onto a crossing. Anyone trying to use it would have to step out into the traffic beside you.
